Stopnica Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stopnica, Poland

Demolished. Between 1754 and 1759, the Seym of the Four Lands — a session of the Council of Four Lands, documented at several other sites in this collection — took place in Stopnica. The town's Jewish population reached 3,226 (75.5 percent) by 1921, most murdered by the Germans at Treblinka in November 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the 17th century alongside the founding of the Jewish community, was liquidated by municipal order in 1958; a Municipal Cooperative building housing a fertilizer warehouse was later erected on the site, and in 2008 a pile of broken tombstones with Hebrew inscriptions was discovered in a nearby private garden.
